parts.label: (a)
parts.text: State what is meant by a magnetic field.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
A long, straight wire P carries a current into the page, as shown in Fig. 6.1.

[[fig:f1]]

On Fig. 6.1, draw four field lines to represent the magnetic field around wire P due to the current in the wire.

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.lead:
A second long, straight wire Q, carrying a current of 5.0 A out of the page, is placed parallel to wire P, as shown in Fig. 6.2.

[[fig:f2]]
parts.text:
The flux density of the magnetic field at wire Q due to the current in wire P is 2.6 mT.

Calculate the magnetic force per unit length exerted on wire Q by wire P.

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.text: State the direction of the force exerted on wire Q by wire P.

parts.label: (c)(iii)
parts.text:
The flux density of the magnetic field at wire P due to the current in wire Q is 1.5 mT.

Determine the magnitude of the current in wire P. Explain your reasoning.

figures.caption: Fig. 6.1
figures.alt: A symbol for a current into the page is connected by a leader to the labels wire P and current into page.

figures.caption: Fig. 6.2
figures.alt: Two parallel wires are shown, with wire P carrying current into the page and wire Q carrying current 5.0 A out of the page.
